clue.text: Tyrant giving drug to small boy

parts.note: Des is a short form of the boy's name Desmond
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Someone hands narcotics to a young lad.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is an absolute ruler wielding power cruelly, a synonym of tyrant.

clue.text: Bud at last seen in first green plant

indicators.note: the bud's final letter is seen inside the next word, so it goes within

parts.note: to come first is to be best

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word bud

parts.note: green means raw, unripe or inexperienced

explanation.surface: A bud finally appears on the first green shoot of a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedstraw is a wild herbaceous plant of the genus Galium, once used to stuff mattresses.

clue.text: Characters potentially OK for crew?

indicators.note: the letters given could potentially be rearranged into other words, signalling a reshuffle

explanation.surface: A question of whether certain people are good enough to man a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A workforce is the body of workers, a crew, and the whole clue describes letters that could form one.

clue.text: What quibblers do about replacing leader in base

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for base is swapped out for another piece

parts.note: base as an adjective means low, wicked, evil
ca is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A description of pedants arguing over something low.
explanation.definitionFit: To cavil is to raise petty objections, which is exactly what quibblers do.

clue.text: Pedestrian's speed when skirting lake on plain

indicators.note: in an across clue on means placed after the preceding piece

parts.note: plain in the sense of ordinary, common

indicators.note: skirting means going round the edge of, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: pace is a rate of speed

explanation.surface: A walker's speed as they skirt a lake on flat ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian as an adjective means dull and ordinary, a synonym of commonplace.

clue.text: Something one trying had in the past

definitions.meaning: someone trying has a go at something, an attempt
earlier, before now, as in years before

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition splits the answer as A GO: when you try, you have a go.
explanation.definitionFit: Ago means in the past, as in 'long ago', and split in two it is an attempt someone had.

clue.text: Scratch the surface of wound, and cause alarm for some

definitions.meaning: to make shallow cuts in skin or loosen topsoil
figuratively, to hurt someone with harsh criticism
an informal usage some speakers have, meaning to frighten

explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition; 'for some' warns that the scaring sense is a nonstandard usage only some people accept.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarify means to scratch or cut a surface, to lacerate with criticism, and informally to frighten.

clue.text: Metal covered by connecting wire

parts.note: lead is a heavy metal
something covered by a coat is in it

explanation.surface: A cable coated with a metallic sheath.
explanation.definitionFit: A lead-in is the wire connecting an aerial to a receiver or transmitter.

clue.text: Great transport, one way or another, for one aboard

indicators.note: a passenger aboard is inside the vehicle, so one piece sits within
the vehicle's name can be read either direction, so here it is taken backwards

parts.note: a bus is a means of public transport
per means for each, as in per person

explanation.surface: Excellent travel arrangements, whichever route, for each passenger on board.
explanation.definitionFit: Superb means excellent or great.

clue.text: Bent Conservative marked for surveillance?

explanation.definitionFit: Cringed means cowered or bent the body in fear, so bent fits as a past tense verb.

clue.text: Turning place for sheep

indicators.note: turning round means the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to place something is to put it

explanation.surface: A spot where flocks turn around.
explanation.definitionFit: A tup is a ram, an uncastrated male sheep.

clue.text: Pretty good show, getting bowled for 100 following on

indicators.note: the show piece follows, coming after the other in the answer

parts.note: re means on or about, regarding

indicators.note: the show gets one letter in place of another, a swap

parts.note: a spectacle is a show or display
C is the Roman numeral for 100
B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled

explanation.surface: A cricketer's decent display, dismissed just short of a century after following on.
explanation.walkthrough: The second C of SPECTACLE becomes B. Following on is a cricket term for batting again straight after a poor first innings.
explanation.definitionFit: Respectable can mean reasonably good or decent in quality, as in a respectable score.

clue.text: Moved close to mother during birth

indicators.note: during means within the time of, so the letter sits inside

parts.note: dawn is the birth or beginning of something

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

explanation.definitionFit: Drawn means pulled or moved, as in drawn towards something.

clue.text: One side of coin given in benefit — there's a catch

explanation.walkthrough: 'There's a catch' sounds like a hidden snag, but the catch is a fish landed.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dover sole is a flatfish, the kind of thing an angler or trawler lands as a catch.

clue.text: Criminal mates pinching your old ring may display it

indicators.note: pinching means grasping between, so one piece is held inside
criminal suggests the letters are wrongly or crookedly arranged

parts.note: thy is the archaic form of your

explanation.surface: Crooks steal your antique ring, which has a jewel set in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' shuffles the letters of mates; 'ring' looks like a crime gang's word but is the jewellery holding the gem.
explanation.definitionFit: Amethyst is a purple gemstone, commonly set in a ring.

clue.text: Spare Times the setter brought back in record time

indicators.note: the pieces are placed in the record, inside it

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
X is the multiplication sign, read as times

indicators.note: brought back means the word is turned round, read in reverse

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves as me

explanation.definitionFit: To spare someone a duty is to exempt them from it.

clue.text: What fledglings do the wrong way round, being despondent

indicators.note: the two halves of the phrase are swapped round, the end going to the front

parts.note: young birds cast down, shedding their first fluffy feathers

explanation.surface: Young birds doing something backwards and feeling low.
explanation.definitionFit: Downcast means low in spirits, a synonym of despondent.

clue.text: Society needs force to beat it

parts.note: to cram is to force or stuff in

explanation.surface: An organisation must use force to win.
explanation.definitionFit: Scram is an informal command to go away, just as beat it is.

clue.text: Fielding side's below par

definitions.meaning: in cricket, one half of the field from the batter's view, opposite the leg side
slightly unwell or not up to standard

explanation.walkthrough: The off side is the half of a cricket field on the side the batter faces.
explanation.definitionFit: The off side is a cricket field area, and feeling off means feeling unwell or below par.

clue.text: Look at what happens when I hit the roof audibly?

indicators.note: audibly signals that the phrase is to be heard, matched by sound

parts.words: what happens when I hit the roof
parts.note: when I hit the roof, get angry, I bawl or yell

explanation.definitionFit: To eyeball something is informally to look at it closely.

clue.text: First-class assessor rising in party's admin office

parts.note: A1 means first-class, with the 1 read as I
a rater is one who assesses or values

explanation.definitionFit: A secretariat is an administrative office or department, as of an organisation.

clue.text: Significant clergyman making sound in the East End?

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a clergyman

parts.note: healing means making well, making sound

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like noise but means healthy. The East End is London's traditional Cockney district.
explanation.definitionFit: Revealing means telling or significant, disclosing something meaningful.

clue.text: Cricket bat badly restricted by variations in pitch

clue.text: Having forgotten answer, decline prize

parts.note: to atrophy is to waste away or decline

explanation.surface: A forgetful contestant turns down an award.
explanation.definitionFit: A trophy is a cup or prize awarded for victory.

clue.text: Green faction's precursor to burying the hatchet?

clue.text: Powerless board as described by a quirky panel

parts.note: qua is Latin for as, in the capacity of

clue.text: Where patient visitors gather, daughter having gone too

parts.note: hospital visitors sit at patients' bedsides

explanation.surface: Hospital visitors gather, though one daughter has left as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patient' looks like an adjective about calm visitors, but is a hospital patient.

clue.text: Clubs will crack

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in cards
to leave something to an heir is to will it

explanation.surface: Weapons will break things open.

clue.text: Backing provides funds for boxing at sports venues

parts.note: to aid a cause is to provide funds for it, so aids

clue.text: Bishop fell over part of cleaner's equipment

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

parts.note: a fell is a moorland hill, a moor

parts.note: X is a cross shape
